newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall, Alcatel posts big gain.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall, Alcatel posts big gain.

text.p: French shares closed lower on Tuesday in the second consecutive fall on doubts about the timetable for European Union as well as due to a weaker dollar and volatile U.S. markets ahead of the FOMC meeting on March 25.

But Alcatel Alsthom posted a closing gain of 8.8 percent to 667 francs, down from a high of 682 francs which was 11 percent up, as analysts upgraded their profit forecasts after a bullish presentation of the 1996 results.
Michelin fell 6.21 percent to 318.50 on disappointment with its results which included big charges.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 14.53 points or 0.56 percent at 2,573.95.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,575 from 2,584 on Monday's close. Volume was 8.7 billion francs of which 6.7 billion in CAC-40 shares.
Brokers and fund managers said that after a price correction the Paris market should resume an upward trend and they see 2,500-2,550 as the objective of the current consolidation.
But they added that a rise would not take place before the March 20 liquidation date for the March trading month and the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25.

Steelmaker Usinor-Sacilor, up 4.4 percent to 89.90 francs, benefitted from the takeover bid in Germany on Thyssen by Krupp which analysts said should lead to a reduction of steel production overcapacity.

Vallourec, down 1.18 percent to 336 francs, said after the close that its 1996 net attributable profit doubled to 196 million francs from 85 million. It said it expected a further rise in profits in 1997.
Total, up 0.02 percent at 457.50, is expected to announce an increase in its 1996 dividend on Wednesday morning to 10 francs from 8.70 francs per share in 1995.
